title: Source of Income Discrimination Prohibition
requirement: Housing providers are prohibited from refusing to rent to someone based on their source of income, applying different terms or conditions based on source of income, or advertising preferences or limitations against sources of income such as Section 8 vouchers.
quoted_span: California law protects tenants from discrimination based on how a tenant will be paying rent (“source of income”).

title: Criminal History Screening Limitations
requirement: Housing providers are prohibited from considering arrests that did not lead to a conviction, sealed or expunged records, juvenile justice records, or having blanket bans on all people with a criminal history.
quoted_span: Housing providers cannot consider some types of criminal history including arrests that did not lead to a conviction, records that are sealed or expunged, or records or matters processed in the juvenile justice system.

title: California Tenant Protection Act of 2019 (AB 1482)
requirement: Annual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region, or 10%, whichever is lower.
exemptions: units constructed within the last 15 years, deed-restricted affordable housing, certain dormitories, owner-occupied two-unit properties, and certain single-family homes/condos
interaction: The JCO does not regulate rent increases, however, state law AB 1482, the California Tenant Protection Act of 2019, may regulate the rent amount in buildings that are older than 15 years old.
quoted_span: Annual rent increases are limited to no more than 5% plus the percentage change in the cost of living for the region in which the property is located, or 10% whichever is lower).
